contentObjective: I can choose the best measure of center for a data set based on its shape.
languageObjective: I can explain my choice using the words mean, median, outlier, and skewed.

vocabulary.definition: A mean, median, or mode chosen because it describes a data set fairly.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una media, mediana o moda elegida porque describe un conjunto de datos de manera justa.
vocabulary.visual: Use the median when an outlier would pull the mean too far.
vocabulary.cloze: A center chosen because it describes the data fairly is an ___ ___ ___ ___.

examples.text: Using the median when one salary is $40 million
examples.why: The outlier drags the mean; the median stays with the group.

examples.text: Using the mean in that same data set
examples.why: One extreme value pulls it away from every actual salary.

vocabulary.definition: The average. Add all the numbers, then divide by how many there are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El promedio. Suma todos los números y divide entre cuántos hay.
vocabulary.cloze: The average of a data set is the ___.

examples.why: Add the values, then divide by how many there are.
That is the total; the mean still needs the division.

vocabulary.definition: The middle number when you put them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número del medio cuando los pones en orden.
vocabulary.cloze: The middle value when data is in order, often best when there is an outlier, is the ___.

examples.why: The middle value once the numbers are in order.
Middle of an unsorted list is not the median.

vocabulary.definition: A number that is much bigger or smaller than the rest.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número mucho mayor o menor que los demás.
vocabulary.visual: Data: 12, 14, 13, 15, 45 → 45 is far from the cluster, so it is an outlier
vocabulary.cloze: A value far from the rest of the data, which can pull the mean, is an ___.

examples.why: It sits far from every other value.
It is the largest, but it is right beside the others.

vocabulary.definition: When most data sits on one side with a tail on the other.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuando la mayoría de los datos está de un lado con una cola del otro.
vocabulary.visual: Scores: 5, 6, 7, 8, 8, 35 → most scores are low, but 35 creates a tail to the right (skewed right)
vocabulary.cloze: Data that is bunched on one side with a tail on the other is ___.

examples.text: Most values low with a few very high values
examples.why: The data has a tail, so it is skewed.

examples.text: Values spread evenly around the center

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.
vocabulary.visual: Symmetric = even on both sides. Skewed = bunched on one side with a tail
vocabulary.cloze: The way data values are spread out is the ___.

examples.text: “Most scores cluster near 85, with one down at 68”
examples.why: It says where the data sits and how it spreads.
One value describes a point, not the shape of the set.

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.
vocabulary.cloze: How much the data values differ is the ___.

examples.why: The values differ, which is what variability measures.
Nothing varies, so there is no spread to describe.

vocabulary.definition: Values bunched close together in one part of a display.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Valores agrupados muy cerca en una parte de la representación.
vocabulary.visual: Values packed near 3 on the dot plot.
vocabulary.cloze: Values bunched close together in one spot form a ___.

examples.text: Twelve dots stacked between 2 and 6 years
examples.why: Many values sit close together in one place.
A single value far away is an outlier, not a cluster.

vocabulary.definition: A space on a display where no data values fall.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un espacio en la representación donde no cae ningún valor de los datos.
vocabulary.visual: Nothing between 11 and 32 on the number line.
vocabulary.cloze: A space where no values fall on a display is a ___.

examples.why: That stretch of the number line holds no data.
That is a place where values do fall.

items.meaning: The middle number when you put them in order

copyPanel.rule: Choosing Appropriate Measures of Center & Spread
steps: 1. Symmetric Data (No Outliers): Use Mean and MAD
2. Skewed Data (Has Outliers): Use Median and IQR (outliers distort the mean)
3. Compare distributions using both center (typical value) and spread (variability)

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Presidential Terms
revealWordProblem.text: A presidential term in the United States is four years. In 1947, Congress passed an amendment to limit the president to two terms. The number of terms served by each president of the United States from 1789 to 2021 is shown in the bar graph. Given this information, what prediction can you make about the number of terms the next U.S. president will serve in office?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A bar graph of the number of presidents who served less than one term, one term, between one and two terms, two terms, and more than two terms.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The graph records a historical data set ending in 2021: fewer than 1 term = 7 presidents, 1 term = 18, between 1 and 2 terms = 3, 2 terms = 15, and more than 2 terms = 1. The frequencies total 44. The modal category is '1 term,' with 18 of 44 observations, or about 40.9%. Based only on the most frequent category in this data set, one possible prediction is 1 term. This is not a guarantee or a measured probability for a future president: a historical frequency does not account for a future election or other circumstances.

questions.stem: A gymnast's scores are: 8.5, 8.8, 8.7, 8.6, 8.9. There are no outliers. Which measure best represents a typical score?
choices: Neither — the data is too small
questions.explanation: The data is symmetric with no outliers, so the mean (8.7) best represents the typical score.
choiceFeedback: The median ignores how far apart the values are. Check whether this data has any outlier that would make leaving values out worthwhile.
Five values is plenty for a measure of center. A small set is only a problem when it contains extreme values.
Both measures actually work reasonably well here, since the scores are clustered close together. Decide which one uses the data most fully when there are no outliers.
hints: Look at the scores: 8.5 up to 8.9 — all five are bunched tightly together with no unusual value.
Rule of thumb: with no outliers and balanced data, one measure uses every value fairly. With outliers, the middle value is safer. Which case is this?
First step: check for an outlier — is any score far from the others? All five sit within 0.4 points, so apply the no-outlier rule.
questions.stemEs: Las puntuaciones de una gimnasta son: 8.5, 8.8, 8.7, 8.6, 8.9. No hay valores atípicos. ¿Cuál medida representa mejor una puntuación típica?
questions.explanationEs: Los datos son simétricos y no tienen valores atípicos, así que la media (8.7) representa mejor la puntuación típica.
choicesEs: Las dos son igual de malas
hintsEs: Mira los puntajes: de 8.5 a 8.9, los cinco muy juntos y sin ningún valor inusual.
Regla práctica: sin valores atípicos y con datos equilibrados, una medida usa todos los valores de forma justa. Con atípicos, el valor del medio es más seguro. ¿Cuál caso es este?
Primer paso: busca un atípico — ¿hay algún puntaje lejos de los demás? Los cinco están dentro de 0.4 puntos, así que aplica la regla de sin atípicos.

questions.stem: A runner's mile times are: 7:10, 7:15, 7:12, 7:20, 12:00. The 12:00 was due to a cramp. Which measure best represents a typical mile?
choices: Mean — it uses all the data
Median — the outlier 12:00 pulls the mean too high
Mode — it shows the most common time
questions.explanation: The 12:00 is an outlier that pulls the mean up. The median (7:15) better represents the runner's typical time.
choiceFeedback: Mean uses all data—but the outlier pulls it too high.
Mode shows most common—but doesn't handle the outlier well.
Both measures exist, but which resists the 12:00 outlier?
hints: Four times are near 7 minutes; one is 12:00 from a cramp. That 12:00 is an outlier, not a typical mile.
Ask: which measure gets dragged toward an extreme value, and which one just takes the middle of the ordered list?
First step: order the times and notice where 12:00 sits — far beyond the rest. Then choose the measure that isn't pulled by that extreme time.
questions.stemEs: Los tiempos de una corredora en la milla son: 7:10, 7:15, 7:12, 7:20, 12:00. El 12:00 se debió a un calambre. ¿Cuál medida representa mejor una milla típica?
questions.explanationEs: El 12:00 es un valor atípico que sube la media. La mediana (7:15) representa mejor el tiempo típico de la corredora.
choicesEs: La media — usa todos los datos
La mediana — el valor atípico de 12:00 sube demasiado la media
La moda — muestra el tiempo más común
hintsEs: Cuatro tiempos rondan los 7 minutos; uno es 12:00 por un calambre. Ese 12:00 es un valor atípico, no una milla típica.
Pregunta: ¿qué medida se deja arrastrar hacia un valor extremo y cuál simplemente toma el medio de la lista ordenada?
Primer paso: ordena los tiempos y fíjate dónde cae 12:00, muy lejos del resto. Luego elige la medida que ese tiempo extremo no jala.

questions.stem: Data set: 5, 6, 7, 7, 8, 50. The mean is about 13.8 and the median is 7. Which better represents the typical value?
choices: Median (7) — the outlier 50 inflates the mean
questions.explanation: The mean (13.8) is higher than 5 of the 6 values because the outlier 50 pulls it up. The median (7) better represents a typical value.
choiceFeedback: Mean uses all data—but 50 pulls it way above 5 of the 6 values.
Both exist, but which is closer to most of the data points?
One works well for typical value—use the one that resists 50.
hints: Five of the six values are between 5 and 8 — then there's 50. Notice where the mean (13.8) lands compared to those five.
Test for 'typical': count how many actual data values sit near 13.8, then how many sit near 7. A good measure stays close to most of the data.
First step: compare 13.8 to the list — it's bigger than 5, 6, 7, 7, AND 8. Ask what pulled it up there, and whether the median has that problem.
questions.stemEs: Conjunto de datos: 5, 6, 7, 7, 8, 50. La media es aproximadamente 13.8 y la mediana es 7. ¿Cuál representa mejor el valor típico?
questions.explanationEs: La media (13.8) es mayor que 5 de los 6 valores porque el valor atípico 50 la jala hacia arriba. La mediana (7) representa mejor un valor típico.
choicesEs: La media (13.8) — incluye todos los valores
Las dos son igual de buenas
La mediana (7) — el valor atípico 50 infla la media
hintsEs: Cinco de los seis valores están entre 5 y 8, y luego está el 50. Fíjate dónde cae la media (13.8) comparada con esos cinco.
Prueba qué es 'típico': cuenta cuántos datos reales están cerca de 13.8 y cuántos cerca de 7. Una buena medida se queda cerca de la mayoría de los datos.
Primer paso: compara 13.8 con la lista — es mayor que 5, 6, 7, 7 Y 8. Pregunta qué la jaló hasta allá y si la mediana tiene ese problema.

reviewHighlights.rule: Choosing Appropriate Measures of Center & Spread
steps: 1. Symmetric Data (No Outliers): Use Mean and MAD
2. Skewed Data (Has Outliers): Use Median and IQR (outliers distort the mean)
3. Compare distributions using both center (typical value) and spread (variability)
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Appropriate Measures is defaulting to the mean just because "it uses all the data," without first checking whether an outlier or skewed shape is present. For example, given a player's points per game 14, 16, 15, 17, 16, 58, a student calculates the mean (136 ÷ 6 ≈ 22.7) and reports that as the typical game — but 58 is far from the cluster of 14–17, so it pulls the mean above 5 of the 6 games. The median (16) actually represents a typical game here. Before choosing a measure, always scan the data for an outlier or a long tail first: only use the mean once you've confirmed the data has neither.

level1.stem: Which measure better shows a typical value for 5, 6, 7, 6, 30: the mean or the median?
level1.stemEs: ¿Qué medida muestra mejor un valor típico de 5, 6, 7, 6, 30: la media o la mediana?
hints: Is one value far from the rest? An outlier pulls the mean toward it.
hintsEs: ¿Hay un valor lejos de los demás? Un valor atípico jala la media hacia él.
level1.explanation: Look for an outlier: 30 Find the mean and the median: 54 ÷ 5 = 10.8; median → 6 Choose the one close to most values: 6
level1.explanationEs: Busca un valor atípico: 30 Halla la media y la mediana: 54 ÷ 5 = 10.8; mediana → 6 Elige la que está cerca de la mayoría de los valores: 6

level1.stem: Which measure should you use for 2, 4, 6, 8, 10: the mean or the median?
level1.stemEs: ¿Qué medida debes usar para 2, 4, 6, 8, 10: la media o la mediana?
hints: Look for a value far from the rest. If there is none, use the mean.
hintsEs: Busca un valor lejos de los demás. Si no hay ninguno, usa la media.
level1.explanation: Look for an outlier: none No outlier, so use the mean: 30 ÷ 5 = 6
level1.explanationEs: Busca un valor atípico: ninguno No hay valor atípico, así que usa la media: 30 ÷ 5 = 6

level1.stem: Which measure better shows a typical value for 20, 22, 21, 23, 2: the mean or the median?
level1.stemEs: ¿Qué medida muestra mejor un valor típico de 20, 22, 21, 23, 2: la media o la mediana?
hints: Is there an outlier? An outlier pulls the mean toward it.
hintsEs: ¿Hay un valor atípico? Un valor atípico jala la media hacia él.
level1.explanation: Look for an outlier: 2 Find the mean and the median: 88 ÷ 5 = 17.6; median → 21 Choose the one close to most values: 21
level1.explanationEs: Busca un valor atípico: 2 Halla la media y la mediana: 88 ÷ 5 = 17.6; mediana → 21 Elige la que está cerca de la mayoría de los valores: 21

level1.stem: Which measure better shows a typical value for 2, 3, 3, 4, 28: the mean or the median?
level1.stemEs: ¿Qué medida muestra mejor un valor típico de 2, 3, 3, 4, 28: la media o la mediana?
hints: Look for a value far from the rest. Does it pull the mean up?
hintsEs: Busca un valor lejos de los demás. ¿Sube la media?
level1.explanation: Look for an outlier: 28 Find the mean and the median: 40 ÷ 5 = 8; median → 3 Choose the one close to most values: 3
level1.explanationEs: Busca un valor atípico: 28 Halla la media y la mediana: 40 ÷ 5 = 8; mediana → 3 Elige la que está cerca de la mayoría de los valores: 3

level1.stem: A player scored 18, 21, 19, 20, 22 and 20 points in 6 games. Which measure should you use for a typical game: the mean or the median?
level1.stemEs: Un jugador anotó 18, 21, 19, 20, 22 y 20 puntos en 6 partidos. ¿Qué medida debes usar para un partido típico: la media o la mediana?
hints: Is any score far from the others? If not, the mean can use every score.
hintsEs: ¿Hay algún puntaje lejos de los demás? Si no, la media puede usar todos los puntajes.
level1.explanation: Look for an outlier: 18 to 22 No outlier, so use the mean: 120 ÷ 6 = 20
level1.explanationEs: Busca un valor atípico: 18 a 22 No hay valor atípico, así que usa la media: 120 ÷ 6 = 20

level2.stem: Sam says the mean is always the best typical value because it uses every number. The data are 6, 7, 7, 8, 32. Is Sam right?
level2.stemEs: Sam dice que la media siempre es el mejor valor típico porque usa todos los números. Los datos son 6, 7, 7, 8, 32. ¿Tiene razón Sam?
hints: Find the mean. Is it close to most of the values?
hintsEs: Halla la media. ¿Está cerca de la mayoría de los valores?
level2.explanation: Find the mean: 60 ÷ 5 = 12 Find the median: 6, 7, 7, 8, 32 → 7 Compare each measure to the values: 12 > 8
level2.explanationEs: Halla la media: 60 ÷ 5 = 12 Halla la mediana: 6, 7, 7, 8, 32 → 7 Compara cada medida con los valores: 12 > 8
choices: No. The outlier 32 pulls the mean up to 12. The median, 7, is better.
Yes. The mean uses every value, so it is always best.
Yes. The mean, 12, is close to most values.
choicesEs: No. El valor atípico 32 sube la media a 12. La mediana, 7, es mejor.
Sí. La media usa todos los valores, así que siempre es la mejor.
Sí. La media, 12, está cerca de la mayoría de los valores.
choiceFeedback: Using every value is the problem here. All of 32 counts, so the mean moves up.
12 is more than 4 of the 5 values. It is not close to most of them.

level2.stem: Which measure better shows a typical value for 1.2, 1.5, 1.4, 1.3, 6.1: the mean or the median?
level2.stemEs: ¿Qué medida muestra mejor un valor típico de 1.2, 1.5, 1.4, 1.3, 6.1: la media o la mediana?
hints: Decimals work the same way. Is one value far from the rest?
hintsEs: Los decimales funcionan igual. ¿Hay un valor lejos de los demás?
level2.explanation: Look for an outlier: 6.1 Find the mean and the median: 11.5 ÷ 5 = 2.3; median → 1.4 Compare each measure to the values: 2.3 > 1.5
level2.explanationEs: Busca un valor atípico: 6.1 Halla la media y la mediana: 11.5 ÷ 5 = 2.3; mediana → 1.4 Compara cada medida con los valores: 2.3 > 1.5

level2.stem: Which measure better shows a typical value for 12, 13, 14, 15, 51: the mean or the median?
level2.stemEs: ¿Qué medida muestra mejor un valor típico de 12, 13, 14, 15, 51: la media o la mediana?
hints: Is there an outlier? An outlier pulls the mean toward it.
hintsEs: ¿Hay un valor atípico? Un valor atípico jala la media hacia él.
level2.explanation: Look for an outlier: 51 Find the mean and the median: 105 ÷ 5 = 21; median → 14 Choose the one close to most values: 14
level2.explanationEs: Busca un valor atípico: 51 Halla la media y la mediana: 105 ÷ 5 = 21; mediana → 14 Elige la que está cerca de la mayoría de los valores: 14

level2.stem: A theater sold 48, 52, 50, 49 and 51 tickets on 5 nights. Which measure should you use for a typical night: the mean or the median?
level2.stemEs: Un teatro vendió 48, 52, 50, 49 y 51 boletos en 5 noches. ¿Qué medida debes usar para una noche típica: la media o la mediana?
hints: Check the shape first. Is any night far from the others?
hintsEs: Primero revisa la forma. ¿Hay alguna noche lejos de las demás?
level2.explanation: Look for an outlier: 48 to 52 No outlier, so use the mean: 250 ÷ 5 = 50
level2.explanationEs: Busca un valor atípico: 48 a 52 No hay valor atípico, así que usa la media: 250 ÷ 5 = 50

level2.stem: A cat weighed 9, 10, 11, 10 and 10 pounds at 5 vet visits. Which measure should the vet use for a typical weight: the mean or the median?
level2.stemEs: Un gato pesó 9, 10, 11, 10 y 10 libras en 5 visitas al veterinario. ¿Qué medida debe usar el veterinario para un peso típico: la media o la mediana?
hints: Check for an outlier first. With no outlier, which measure uses every value?
hintsEs: Primero busca un valor atípico. Si no hay, ¿qué medida usa todos los valores?
level2.explanation: Look for an outlier: 9 to 11 No outlier, so use the mean: 50 ÷ 5 = 10
level2.explanationEs: Busca un valor atípico: 9 a 11 No hay valor atípico, así que usa la media: 50 ÷ 5 = 10

level3.stem: A data set of house prices contains one mansion worth far more than every other home. Which pair of measures best describes this data?
choiceFeedback: The mansion drags the mean upward, and MAD measures distance from that pulled mean, so both are distorted.
Range is the maximum minus the minimum, so the mansion sets it by itself, and it pulls the mean too.
Mode is the most frequent price, which says nothing about the middle, and the range is set by the mansion alone.
level3.explanation: The mansion is an outlier that pulls the mean upward and inflates the range. The median and IQR describe the middle of the data and are resistant to a single extreme value.

level3.stem: Set P is 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Set Q is 10, 12, 14, 16, 80. Which set needs the median to show a typical value?
level3.stemEs: El conjunto P es 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. El conjunto Q es 10, 12, 14, 16, 80. ¿Qué conjunto necesita la mediana para mostrar un valor típico?
hints: Look at the shape of each set. Which one has a value far from the rest?
hintsEs: Mira la forma de cada conjunto. ¿Cuál tiene un valor lejos de los demás?
level3.explanation: Look for an outlier in each set: P: none → Q: 80 Find the mean and the median of Q: 132 ÷ 5 = 26.4; median → 14
level3.explanationEs: Busca un valor atípico en cada conjunto: P: ninguno → Q: 80 Halla la media y la mediana de Q: 132 ÷ 5 = 26.4; mediana → 14
choiceFeedback: Set P has no outlier. Its values are evenly spaced, so the mean fits.
Only Set Q has a value far from the rest.
80 is far from the rest of Set Q. It pulls the mean up to 26.4.

level3.stem: Which measure better shows a typical value for 40, 44, 42, 43, 41, 5: the mean or the median?
level3.stemEs: ¿Qué medida muestra mejor un valor típico de 40, 44, 42, 43, 41, 5: la media o la mediana?
hints: Is the outlier high or low? Which way does it pull the mean?
hintsEs: ¿El valor atípico es alto o bajo? ¿Hacia dónde jala la media?
level3.explanation: Look for an outlier: 5 Find the mean and the median: 215 ÷ 6 ≈ 35.8; (41 + 42) ÷ 2 = 41.5 Compare each measure to the values: 35.8 < 40
level3.explanationEs: Busca un valor atípico: 5 Halla la media y la mediana: 215 ÷ 6 ≈ 35.8; (41 + 42) ÷ 2 = 41.5 Compara cada medida con los valores: 35.8 < 40

level3.stem: Mo's trips to school took 15, 18, 16, 17, 14 and 60 minutes. The 60 was a snow day. Give the best typical time.
level3.stemEs: Los viajes de Mo a la escuela duraron 15, 18, 16, 17, 14 y 60 minutos. El de 60 fue un día de nieve. Da el mejor tiempo típico.
hints: Decide on the measure first. With 6 values, use the 3rd and 4th values in order.
hintsEs: Primero decide la medida. Con 6 valores, usa el 3.º y el 4.º valor en orden.
level3.explanation: Look for an outlier: 60 Choose the median. Order the values: 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 60 Find the median: (16 + 17) ÷ 2 = 16.5
level3.explanationEs: Busca un valor atípico: 60 Elige la mediana. Ordena los valores: 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 60 Halla la mediana: (16 + 17) ÷ 2 = 16.5

level3.stem: Six values have a mean of 20 and a median of 12. Does the data most likely have a high outlier, a low outlier, or no outlier?
level3.stemEs: Seis valores tienen una media de 20 y una mediana de 12. ¿Es más probable que los datos tengan un valor atípico alto, uno bajo o ninguno?
hints: An outlier pulls the mean toward it. Which way was this mean pulled?
hintsEs: Un valor atípico jala la media hacia él. ¿Hacia dónde fue jalada esta media?
level3.explanation: Compare the mean to the median: 20 > 12 The mean was pulled up. Name the cause: high outlier
level3.explanationEs: Compara la media con la mediana: 20 > 12 La media fue jalada hacia arriba. Nombra la causa: valor atípico alto
choiceFeedback: A low outlier pulls the mean down, so the mean would be less than the median.
With no outlier, the mean and median are usually close. 20 and 12 are far apart.
